author: Ken
text:
Ken wrote: I was going to post this earlier but been held back by other stuff..

I like to hear your views.. how you'd analyze 3 gu shorts.. entries and exits.. what u see.. would u have taken these trades on and so on..

Thx guys.. nice analysis..

One question i was looking somebody to ask positions size. After all I took a bit of adventures trade on with the first entry as there was no PA config at the entry point..

When I take on this kind of trades i start with small position. in this case first entry was 0.5 second std 1 lot and third one was 2 lots. However, stops for the second and the third entry were just above the previous peak while for the first entry it was just above the h4 supply.

My trading mainly based on spotting where noticeable buyers and sellers are.. all other tech stuff comes after.

Keep in mind position sizing must be relevant to your account size. My view is that if you open a micro account it should be at least $5.000, for trading mini lots it shouldn't be less than $20.000 and for standard lots $100k + if you want want to survive and possibly get somewhere in markets.

Whiteout, there are times I risk up-to 5% but I try to keep it around 2% for any one of my accounts.

Sometimes, I have 10 or 15 open trades running with any one account. Then some may ask how the heck I can keep it within 2-5% account risk ratio. No, I don't have zillion $ accounts. Once any one of my trades locked, means at least stop moved to be +spread then that trade is no longer included in my risk pool.

One day I'll try to put together an article about "Risk Management" if and when I get around to do it. Risk management is THE Holly Grail of trading.
